summary: Vice President JD Vance made headlines this week by publicly stating he's "obsessed" with accessing UFO files and describing extraterrestrials as "demons," prompting a response from Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb on the theological framing. Meanwhile, the ongoing 3I/ATLAS mystery deepened with reports of nuclear fuel signatures, and journalist Ross Coulthart continued investigating the disappearance of General Keith McCasland, suggesting possible foul play and noting the former UFO authority was never seen leaving his home. On the broader whistleblower front, a former security analyst confirmed that UFO insiders have long reported feeling threatened, while an ex-Air Force officer came forward with Cold War-era accounts of UFO activity at a Montana nuclear base. The government's disclosure apparatus continues to move on its own timeline: the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act includes a UAP briefing deadline set for June 30, and several previously unreleased UAP documents were added to the archives this week, including the 2025 AARO trifold briefing.
